questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a spanish speaking country, and I had already been in Granada, and I love the culture and atmosphere in Andalucia!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been the best time of my life! I have met my best friends from all over the world

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult, because the webpage of university of Granada is a bit messy, but there is a list of things, that you have to know on their website and you can always right the international office an email if you have questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation day at the faculty where they helped you creating the emails and accounts you need. At the beginning it was quite confusing, but you will learn it quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was a bit complicated when you had to change your courses, and I recommend you doing it with a friend, so you can help each other out. Other wise they are very helpful at the international office at the faculty. There is such an office at each faculty.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are some residences nearby my faculty filosofia y letras in cartuja called: Carlos V, Amro, Livensa living and maybe more. I stayed at Amro which was only a 3 min walk to the faculty. It was very good but expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had my own kitchen, but you can also choose to get food at the cafeteria on the residence. And the faculty filosofia y letras has a very nice cafeteria with many cheap options.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's very practical because it's close to the university in cartuja, but around 30 min to walk to the centre. But you can also take a bus to the centre that is fast. But in the night time there are no busses so you have to walk or take a taxi, which is cheap. And it's so safe to walk in the night, I have never felt so safe in any other place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The residences are very convenient but very expensive in comparison with the apartments.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arrival you have chosen 5 courses each 6 ects on your learning agreement, and if you want to change them you have to do it in an excel programme that they will explain to you upon arrival. And then they have to sign your final learning agreement with the actual courses you took.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could always go to the international office either physically or write them an email, but I recommend you going there in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I attended all of the classes I wanted. But it was difficult to find courses that did not overlap with the timetables.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want to change courses do not do it at the last moment as I did and do it with a friend so you can help each other out. And be aware of the opening hours of the international office that closes around 14 o'clock maybe.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very different from the university in Copenhagen. I felt like being back in high school because we did not have big lectures but class rooms, where you just have to listen to the teacher and take notes. There is homework and papers you have to hand in, but it's not as difficult as in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a good level because they were easier than the ones I have in Copenhagen which was perfect considering they were in Spanish.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As I have already described there is less interaction with the teacher, but it also depends on the teacher if he or she wants inputs or if you should just listen. And it's also important coming to the classes and they sometimes check who is attending, as you are only allowed a certain percentage of absence in order to pass the class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduccion a la psicologia (at anthropology)
Español como lengua extranjera (at centro de lenguas modernas)
Métodos y técnicas de investigacion de antropologia
Developmental psychology (at the faculty of education)
Historia del arte y patrimonio historico (anthropology)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i liked the class Métodos y técnicas de investigacion de antropologia which was the most anthropological one where you get to make 2 interviews in spanish on a theme you choose to investigate. History of art was also interesting and the teacher Adrian was very good. I really recommen español como lengua extranjera as you take it with other exchange students and it's an easier class than the other courses and there is a nice environment in the class and very god teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The laundry was 3€ and the dryer was 2,5€ at my residence.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The taxis were cheap. But I travelled a lot to different cities and the busses can be a bit expensive. But I recommend you using blablacar or Amovens where you share a car with other people and it's faster than the bus.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did yoga twice a week and took dancing classes twice a week (bachata and salsa). There are so many options!! the yoga classes where through the university at casa de porras which is very cheap.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university has a cultural centre called casa de porras, where there is all kinds of activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved dancing and you can also go to the gym, play padel tennis, go swimming, go hiking, do ceramics, yoga, meditiation and many more activites.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go out eating tapas that you get for free with your drink. 
Go on the trips organized by Best life experience, Emycet and ESN, which is guided and transportation is included and it's cheaper than going on your own. 
Go to the beautiful viewpoints san miguel alto and san nicolas in Albaicin. 
Go to the live music places at eshavira club, planta baja, bohemia jazz cafe and there are many more.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy! I felt more at home than in Denmark

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
In your classes the spanish students don't always talk to you so approach them and say hi! You have nothing to lose!
It's very easy making friends with other exchange students through the events of best life experience, emycet and esn

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Everything is closed in sundays and also everyday around 14-17 o'clock

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go there with an open mind where you will meet many new people from all over the world. Expect som long days at uni where they don't give you breaks, but it's worth it when you have the best freetime ever without much sleep.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should get a permission of residence called NIE at the oficina de extranjeria of the municipality (ayuntamiento). You can ask the international office of the information.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing people and I really loved going dancing bachata and salsa and they developed my spanish language skills a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: At the beginning it was difficult understanding the professors in spanish, because they also wore a mask. But you will get used to it quickly.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
